lots.what_it_is: Framed colour print 'Supercharged to the Max' (Mad Max V8 Interceptor, 1973 XB GT Ford Falcon Coupe) by Mike Harbar, black and gold frame, under glass.

sold.note: kind SOLD, currency AUD, no conversion. same_item: close. API record opened and lot photo viewed: 'Framed Mike Harbar Print - Mountain Rivals', the 1981 James Hardie 1000 Bathurst image (Johnson/French Falcon v Brock Commodore), silver frame, printed signature in the image. Same artist, same print format and caption style, but a different image (Bathurst, not Mad Max; the researcher wrongly called it a cycling scene). Hammer only, premium extra.

lots.guide_summary: One close SOLD entry only: a different Mike Harbar print in the same format made $100 hammer at Gowans in Aug 2026. No same-image sold, unsold or asking evidence could be found (web search budget used up, artist site blocked by the proxy). All AUD.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD entry: the only sale is a different Harbar image (Mountain Rivals), so under the rules no maximum is set. For guidance only: if that sale were treated as same-item, keep would be 100 / 1.198 = 83.5, so $80, and flip from a $100 resale less about 13.4% fees ($13) and $35 postage for a glazed frame = $52 / 2.396 = $21.7, so $20. The Mad Max subject may draw more interest than Bathurst, but that is untested.
lots.confidence_reason: Artist and title read from the printed caption and the lot title, but only one close (not same) sale, and it is a different image. Open print versus limited edition is not confirmed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged lower left: the signature is part of the printed image (sits on the painted road line), not a pencil signature in the margin. No edition number visible in the margins. Caption reads 'SUPERCHARGED TO THE MAX / Mad Max V8 Interceptor / 1973 XB GT Ford Falcon Coupe'. Heavy window glare across the glass. Frame looks sound in the one photo.
lots.condition: Appears sound from one glare-affected photo; glass, frame corners and back not seen. Likely an open decorative print with printed signature.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there a pencil signature or edition number in the margin under the mount, or a certificate or label on the back? Any chips to the frame or cracks in the glass?
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. The researcher's entry URL was the search endpoint; I replaced it with the direct lot record (431052) after opening it, and corrected the subject from 'cycling or mountain scene' to the 1981 Bathurst cars image. Kept as close, not same item.

lots.guide_summary: All SOLD, all Gowans hammers (premium extra), Oct 2025 to Sep 2026: console with controllers $70 to $95, bare console $60, bundles with several games $110 to $140. No unsold or asking entries. All AUD.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in 24 months = $70 (lot 375809, console, cords and one controller, Nov 2025). 70 / 1.198 = 58.4, rounded down to $55 (all-in about $66). The bare-console $60 sale is excluded as a lesser lot. Flip: likely resale about $95 (top of the console-plus-controllers sales, e.g. 403404), sold locally on Marketplace with no fee and buyer collecting. 95 / 2.396 = 39.6, rounded down to $35. Selling posted on eBay (13.4% fee $13 plus about $25 postage) leaves $57 / 2.396 = $23.8, so $20. Recent Gowans hammers of $70 to $95 mean a $35 flip bid is unlikely to win.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification clear (Sony and PlayStation marks read on controllers and console) and many opened Gowans SOLD records, but the lot is untested and the past lots have no descriptions, so condition comparability is uncertain.
lots.key_photo_findings: Grey PS1 (lid-style top loader) with power and AV leads, one grey digital Sony controller and one Sony DualShock analog controller, Crash Bandicoot 3 Warped Platinum disc in a cracked-corner jewel case on top. Model number underneath not visible. No box or memory card.
lots.condition: Untested; cosmetically average for age from one photo. Disc condition unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: Has it been powered up and does it read discs? Is the Crash disc scratched, and is there a memory card?
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped; all 8 Gowans records reopened and title, hammer and bid count match the researcher. Same_item upgraded to 'yes' for the four console-plus-controller lots; bare console and big bundles left as close.

lots.guide_summary: Mostly SOLD: eBay sales recorded on PriceCharting's PAL page, CIB US$22 to US$45 (A$32 to A$65) in the last 24 months, sealed US$76 (A$109). One ASKING guide figure (CIB US$47.84, A$68). No Gowans history. Rate 1 USD = 1.43 AUD. A US$12.79 CIB sale (Jun 2025) was left out as an outlier.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item CIB SOLD in 24 months (excluding the US$12.79 outlier) = US$22.13 x 1.43 = A$31.65; 31.65 / 1.198 = 26.4, rounded down to $25. Flip: likely resale US$34 x 1.43 = A$48.6, less eBay AU fees about 13.4% ($6.50) and postage for a boxed figure about $15 = $27.1; 27.1 / 2.396 = 11.3, rounded down to $10. Only worth it if the game cartridge is inside.
lots.confidence_reason: Box clearly read, and several sold prices seen on an opened PriceCharting page, but they are eBay sales seen second-hand, and whether the game and all inserts are inside is unknown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Front of the window box only: 'Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle Collector's Edition', Nintendo Switch logo, Australian G classification, Ubisoft logo, Rabbid Mario figure visible in the plastic tray. The open flap at right belongs to a separate red box behind it, not this lot. Box front looks clean with light shelf wear. No view of the back, seal or game case.
lots.condition: Box front looks good with light shelf wear; sealed or opened is unknown. Contents beyond the figure not confirmed.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the Switch game cartridge and case inside the box, along with any inserts? Is the figure complete and undamaged?
